context.guidance: Do not write Personal Data or Authentication Secrets to localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies or outbound headers beyond what the session strictly needs. Keep identity in an opaque session identifier held server-side, and keep only non-Personal Data preferences in the browser. Where a value must be held client-side, protect it as Rule 6(1)(a) requires.

value.fix: Stop persisting the authentication token in localStorage. Remove `localStorage.setItem('token', authentication.token)` and have the server issue an opaque session identifier in an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict (or Lax) cookie, with the identity and token kept server-side in a session store. The client should not read or store the token. If a client-side credential is unavoidable, keep it in memory only, make it short-lived, and protect it as Rule 6(1)(a) requires. Keep only non-Personal Data preferences such as theme or locale in browser storage. On logout and on existing sessions, delete any previously stored `token` key from localStorage (`localStorage.removeItem('token')`) and invalidate the server-side session. Finally, verify that the login flow still authenticates, that the token no longer appears in localStorage in DevTools, and that the session is cleared on logout.
